# captured 2026-09-22
# exe: /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/rustic
# args: 
rustic - fast, encrypted, deduplicated backups powered by Rust

Usage: rustic [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  backup       Backup to the repository
  cat          Show raw data of files and blobs in a repository
  config       Change the repository configuration
  completions  Generate shell completions
  check        Check the repository
  copy         Copy snapshots to other repositories
  diff         Compare two snapshots or paths
  docs         Open the documentation
  dump         Dump the contents of a file within a snapshot to stdout
  find         Find patterns in given snapshots
  forget       Remove snapshots from the repository
  init         Initialize a new repository
  key          Manage keys for a repository
  list         List repository files by file type
  ls           List file contents of a snapshot
  merge        Merge snapshots
  snapshots    Show a detailed overview of the snapshots within the repository
  show-config  Show the configuration which has been read from the config file(s)
  self-update  Update to the latest stable rustic release
  prune        Remove unused data or repack repository pack files
  restore      Restore (a path within) a snapshot
  rewrite      Rewrite existing snapshot(s)
  repair       Repair a snapshot or the repository index
  repoinfo     Show general information about the repository
  tag          Change tags of snapshots
  webdav       Start a webdav server which allows to access the repository
  version      Print version information
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Global options:
      --profile-substitute-env
          Substitute environment variables in profiles
          
          [env: RUSTIC_PROFILE_SUBSTITUTE_ENV=]

  -P, --use-profile <PROFILE>
          Config profile to use. This parses the file `<PROFILE>.toml` in the config directory.
          [default: "rustic"]
          
          [env: RUSTIC_USE_PROFILE=]

  -g, --group-by <CRITERION>
          Group snapshots by any combination of host,label,paths,tags, e.g. to find the latest
          snapshot [default: "host,label,paths"]
          
          [env: RUSTIC_GROUP_BY=]

  -n, --dry-run
          Only show what would be done without modifying anything. Does not affect read-only
          commands
          
          [env: RUSTIC_DRY_RUN=]

      --dry-run-warmup
          Additional to dry run, but still issue warm-up command if configured
          
          [env: RUSTIC_DRY_RUN_WARMUP=]

      --check-index
          Check if index matches pack files and read pack headers if necessary
          
          [env: RUSTIC_CHECK_INDEX=]

      --log-level <LOG_LEVEL>
          Use this log level [default: info]
          
          [env: RUSTIC_LOG_LEVEL=]
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

      --log-level-logfile <LOG_LEVEL_LOGFILE>
          Use this log level for the log file [default: info]
          
          [env: RUSTIC_LOG_LEVEL_LOGFILE=]
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

      --log-level-dryrun <LOG_LEVEL_DRYRUN>
          Use this log level in dry-run mode [default: info]
          
          [env: RUSTIC_LOG_LEVEL_DRYRUN=]
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

      --log-level-dependencies <LOG_LEVEL_DEPENDENCIES>
          Use this log level for dependencies [default: warn]
          
          [env: RUSTIC_LOG_LEVEL_DEPENDENCIES=]
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

      --log-file <LOGFILE>
          Write log messages to the given file (using log-level-logfile)
          
          [env: RUSTIC_LOG_FILE=]

      --no-progress
          Don't show any progress bar
          
          [env: RUSTIC_NO_PROGRESS=]

      --json-progress
          Write progress as newline-delimited JSON
          
          [env: RUSTIC_JSON_PROGRESS=]

      --progress-interval <DURATION>
          Interval to update progress bars (default: 100ms)
          
          [env: RUSTIC_PROGRESS_INTERVAL=]

      --prometheus <PUSHGATEWAY_URL>
          Push metrics to a Prometheus Pushgateway
          
          [env: RUSTIC_PROMETHEUS=]

      --prometheus-user <USER>
          Authenticate to Prometheus Pushgateway using this user
          
          [env: RUSTIC_PROMETHEUS_USER=]

      --prometheus-pass <PASSWORD>
          Authenticate to Prometheus Pushgateway using this password
          
          [env: RUSTIC_PROMETHEUS_PASS=]

      --opentelemetry <ENDPOINT_URL>
          OpenTelemetry metrics endpoint (HTTP Protobuf)
          
          [env: RUSTIC_OTEL=]

      --show-time-offset
          Show time offsets instead of converting to system time zone
          
          [env: RUSTIC_SHOW_TIME_OFFSET=]

Repository options:
  -r, --repository <REPOSITORY>
          Repository to use
          
          [env: RUSTIC_REPOSITORY=]
          [alias: --repo]

      --repo-hot <REPO_HOT>
          Repository to use as hot storage
          
          [env: RUSTIC_REPO_HOT=]

      --no-cache
          Don't use a cache
          
          [env: RUSTIC_NO_CACHE=]

      --cache-dir <CACHE_DIR>
          Use this dir as cache dir instead of the standard cache dir
          
          [env: RUSTIC_CACHE_DIR=]

      --warm-up
          Warm up needed data pack files by only requesting them without processing

      --warm-up-command <WARM_UP_COMMAND>
          Warm up needed data pack files by running the command with %id replaced by pack id

      --warm-up-wait-command <WARM_UP_WAIT_COMMAND>
          Wait for end of warm up by running the command with %id replaced by pack id

      --warm-up-wait <DURATION>
          Duration (e.g. 10m) to wait after warm up

      --warm-up-batch <WARM_UP_BATCH>
          Batch size for warm-up command invocations

credential options:
      --key <KEY>
          masterkey to use
          
          [env: RUSTIC_KEY]

      --key-file <KEY_FILE>
          File to read the masterkey from
          
          [env: RUSTIC_KEY_FILE=]

      --key-command <KEY_COMMAND>
          Command to read the masterkey from. Key is read from stdout
          
          [env: RUSTIC_KEY_COMMAND=]

      --password <PASSWORD>
          Password for the repository
          
          # Warning
          
          * Using --password can reveal the password in the process list!
          
          [env: RUSTIC_PASSWORD]

  -p, --password-file <PASSWORD_FILE>
          File to read the password from
          
          [env: RUSTIC_PASSWORD_FILE=]

      --password-command <PASSWORD_COMMAND>
          Command to read the password from. Password is read from stdout
          
          [env: RUSTIC_PASSWORD_COMMAND=]

Snapshot filter options:
      --filter-host <HOSTNAME>
          Hostname to filter (can be specified multiple times)

      --filter-label <LABEL>
          Label to filter (can be specified multiple times)

      --filter-paths <PATH[,PATH,..]>
          Path list to filter (can be specified multiple times)

      --filter-paths-exact <PATH[,PATH,..]>
          Path list to filter exactly (no superset) as given (can be specified multiple times)

      --filter-tags <TAG[,TAG,..]>
          Tag list to filter (can be specified multiple times)

      --filter-tags-exact <TAG[,TAG,..]>
          Tag list to filter exactly (no superset) as given (can be specified multiple times)

      --filter-after <DATE(TIME)>
          Only use snapshots which are taken after the given given date/time

      --filter-before <DATE(TIME)>
          Only use snapshots which are taken before the given given date/time

      --filter-size <SIZE>
          Only use snapshots with total size in given range

      --filter-size-added <SIZE>
          Only use snapshots with size added to the repo in given range

      --filter-last <COUNT>
          Only use the last COUNT snapshots for each group

      --filter-jq <JQ>
          jq to filter snapshots
